biggest_catch: $0 annual fee, so the 20,000 points are pure upside on the fee side — the traps are the five-year same-product ban and the 90-day clock. If you got this card's bonus in the last five years, there is no bonus at all. Only eligible net purchases count toward the $1,000, so keep it to spending you already planned — never buy extra to fill the gap. Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, and carrying a balance at the card's ~20%+ variable APR erases the points' value fast — pay in full every month.
catches: Only pursue spending you already planned to do — never buy extra things just to hit a bonus threshold; overspending to chase a bonus wipes out the bonus math and is how people lose money on it.
The five-year same-product rule is strict: current or previous cardmembers who received this product's bonus in the past five years get nothing.
Only eligible net purchases count — returns, fees, and cash-like transactions do not move you toward the $1,000.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily dip your credit score by a few points.
The card's variable APR (~20%+) will erase the points' value fast if you carry a balance — pay the full statement balance every month.

steps: Go to the official U.S. Bank Altitude Connect page and read the 20,000-point / $1,000 / 90-day terms.
Apply online and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Spend $1,000 in eligible net purchases — your already-planned spending — within the first 90 days.
Pay the full statement balance every month so interest never eats the bonus.
Confirm the 20,000 bonus points credit within 1–2 billing cycles after you qualify.
